source.title: A Dominant Diffuse Phase in the Sparse Autoencoder Phase Diagram

page_placements.theme: SAE objectives admit low-loss solutions that differ from the true features (theory and toy)

record.tranche_reason: The study measures a controlled synthetic SAE setting and reports a diffuse regime rather than the expected recovery or merging; its results refine or challenge the proposed splitting and absorption patterns.
record.gate_note: The study reports results from 200 canonical full-batch fits and a 3,300-fit minibatch companion grid. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results. The paper's full-batch measurements cover only 10 of 165 cells; the companion grid covers all cells with a different optimizer.
record.test_reason: In a controlled synthetic nested-feature generator, the study measures splits (several atoms on one true feature) across dictionary sizes and absorption-type pairwise merges across nesting levels. It finds no merges, even at γ=1, and splits only at M=512. It argues trained SAEs fall in a diffuse regime outside the recovery-versus-merging framing.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find a reproducible diffuse trained regime: near-perfect reconstruction, weak alignment, dense codes, and no recoveries or merges, robust to 2× training and minibatch Adam. They conclude that trained amortized SAEs differ from two-feature exact-coding minimizers, which provably merge nested features. They also warn that reconstruction quality does not certify feature recovery.
record.recipe_differences: A controlled synthetic nested-support dictionary, centered ReLU encoder, unit-norm decoder and ℓ1 penalty; the canonical protocol uses full-batch Adam, with a separate minibatch companion grid. It measures predefined recovery, merge and split outcomes rather than studying features in language-model activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different alignment with changes in λ and dictionary size; the nesting fraction has little reported effect on alignment in the measured canonical slice. The canonical γ change also changes child-feature frequency, confounding dependence and rarity. The minibatch optimizer reaches a similar plateau to full-batch training.

fits_no_version.finding: Trained vanilla ℓ1 SAEs reconstruct near-perfectly but recover few true features: matched fraction ≤0.036 canonical and ≤0.046 in the minibatch grid. Median best cosine is 0.47–0.73 and codes are 10–28× denser than ground truth. Alignment rises with M and peaks at an interior λ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs trained on dense superposed synthetic data can enter a diffuse phase in which reconstruction quality does not imply feature recovery.

record.problems: The canonical full-batch experiment measures only 10 of 165 cells and uses one fixed synthetic dictionary and associated datasets. The γ intervention confounds nesting dependence with child-feature rarity. The companion grid uses a different optimizer. The authors note that their pairwise merge threshold does not settle whether trained solutions reach global minima of the amortized objective.
record.rows_left_out: No per-cell numerical values were extracted from the minibatch Figure 4 beyond values explicitly stated in the text; the text reports aggregate grid findings instead. The paper does not report input-partition tests for its detected splits.

untested.parts: Whether split atoms are finer features covering subsets of the parent's inputs. The synthetic true features have no finer sub-features, so splits here are near-duplicate atoms.
No language models or open SAE releases are evaluated.
No nested feature families or hierarchy-mirroring geometry are measured.
Latent firing behaviour (parent failing to fire when a child is active) is not measured; only a geometric decoder merge criterion is used.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, and no count of novel latents.
Only vanilla ReLU+ℓ1 is trained. There is no Matryoshka or other objective comparison, split counts are not reported by γ, and no model's own units are examined.

missing.what: Per-cell merge outcome at γ=1.0, where every feature belongs to a nested pair: zero merges. It is aggregated into R31 but is the strongest V4-relevant condition.
missing.locator: Section 5, 'Nesting has almost no effect'; Table 1

missing.what: Split counts by γ in the companion grid are not reported, so it is unknown whether splitting depends on nesting. This is a paper limitation, not a row omission.

record.verdict_notes: The study's 'split' means duplicate atoms on an atomic ground-truth feature, not coarse-to-fine splitting. V6's links and label were removed: only one objective is used, splits are not broken down by γ, and no model's own units exist here. The V4 merge test is geometric, and absent merges co-occur with absent alignment, so the result is labelled limits_scope rather than challenges. The γ axis confounds nesting with child rarity.

versions.untested_parts: The study detects splitting using multiple atoms closely aligned to one known feature; it does not test whether those atoms partition that feature's inputs into more-specific subsets.
No large language models or open SAE releases are evaluated.
The study does not test nested feature families or whether their geometry mirrors a conceptual hierarchy.
The study tests a pairwise geometric merge criterion on nested synthetic features, not whether a parent latent fails to activate on inputs where a child takes over.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, or count of novel latents, is measured.
The study measures splitting under one vanilla ReLU plus ℓ1 objective, but does not compare objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs or test whether SAE features reflect a model's own units.

relationships.reason: Splits appear only at the larger dictionary, consistent with growth, but weakly. There are none in any M=256 canonical cell (R21–R29), 5/20 runs at M=512 (R30), and at most 30% of runs in 34 companion-grid cells (R33).
relationships.display_finding: No splits appeared in any M=256 canonical cell, splits appeared in 5 of 20 runs at M=512, and at most 30% of runs split in 34 companion-grid cells.

relation.reason: Its own measurements of splits and merges bear on V1 and V4, though in a different regime.

tranche.reason: Results show the absorption and splitting pictures are partial or regime-dependent. The paper frames its null as tension with toy absorption and splitting results. 'Complements, not contradicts' still means partial, which fits T5 and both limits_scope verdicts.

source_check.notes: Clean text, Table 1 aligns. 'Split' means two or more live atoms at cosine ≥0.95 to one true feature (no finer sub-features exist). 'Merge' is a geometric decoder criterion, not latent firing. Matched-fraction maxima (0.036, 0.046) come from Table 1 (M=512) and Section 6, not R1-R3.

statements.problem: Accurate. Minor: the parenthetical ranges (γ 0.0-1.0; λ 10^-4 to 10^-2) span a cross-shaped slice of nine M=256 cells, not a full γ×λ grid.
The sentence is accurate. Context: the one split cell differs from its M=256 twin by M, not λ. No λ (10^-4 to 10^-2) gave splits at M=256.

statements.correction: Table 1: 0 splits at γ=0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0 (M=256, λ=10^-2). Alignment: γ≤0.5 indistinguishable, mild decline at γ≥0.8. Grid: 34 cells with splits, per-γ breakdown not given; peak matched fractions 0.046 (γ=0) vs 0.045 (γ=1).
statements.problem: The alignment part is right. 'Split counts by γ are not reported' is wrong for the canonical slice: Table 1 gives 0 splits at each γ. Per-γ split counts are missing only for the grid.
Makes no claim about this study.
Makes no claim about this study.

All numbers match the text: ≤0.036 canonical, ≤0.046 grid, cosine 0.472-0.727, density 9.9-27.9x (conclusion: 'roughly 10-28x'). R1-R3 support only the low end; the maxima come from Table 1 and Section 6.
